get.description:
List all documents in a project.

``project_id`` was not a parameter, so the r4 client's project (``r4 rag
docs <project>``, ``/rag docs <project>``) was dropped and the caller's own
corpus listed under it (TUI audit 2026-10-17). It now names the corpus,
checked like ``/query``: read tier, then the ADR-080 access list.

K1.3 (2026-10-24): with the central upload facade (the default) the
documents are the spine's artifacts this caller may read (``_rag_spine``);
the endpoint corpus answered ``[]`` after every upload.

post.description:
Answer a question: the knowledge spine first, per UMRS_RAG_QUERY_FACADE.

Uploads feed only the spine (WP-15), so the endpoint corpus alone could
never answer from them.

Upload a document for RAG indexing.

WP-15 dual-corpus dwell (owner decision 2026-09-11): NEW uploads write
to the CENTRAL durable ingest plane at ``/umrs/knowledge/upload``;
the endpoint-corpus proxy stays available only behind the explicit
``UMRS_RAG_UPLOAD_FACADE=endpoint`` opt-in (endpoint corpus is read-only
for standing data). There is no silent dual-write.

post.description:
Start the run a plan describes (ADR-105 D-4): verify the signature,
expiry and caller, re-resolve (a changed target is ``plan_stale``), check
``auto`` against the project's threshold, then trigger with the plan id
as the idempotency key: a second commit answers the run already started.
The project's ``require_plan`` does not apply here.
# auth: verified

Resolve and sign a run plan (ADR-105 D-4). The same identity,
authorization, resolution and parameter validation as trigger; nothing
is written (no job, no catalog change). Commit before ``expires_at``.

Start a run. Refused (typed 403 ``workflows.plan_required``) when the
project requires plan -> commit (ADR-105 D-4); a work level's request
needs its scope's ``workflow:<name>`` grant (ADR-108 D-3).
